details:
Martian Expedition Intelligence

Martian Expedition Intelligence is a planetary exploration and traverse-planning platform developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It helps users investigate scientifically significant regions of Mars and compare potential expedition routes using geological evidence, terrain information, and scientific observations.

The project focuses on Jezero Crater, a region of particular scientific interest because of its ancient lake environment, delta deposits, and potential evidence of past water activity. It organizes exploration targets into a structured portfolio, connecting geological descriptions with available scientific datasets, interpretations, confidence levels, and alternative explanations.

The platform combines multiple layers of planetary information, including Viking MDIM 2.1 imagery, MOLA elevation and relief products, and CRISM mineralogical observations. It also explores two expedition concepts: a full basin rim-to-floor transect and a paleolake hydrological loop. These routes allow users to compare distance, elevation gain, and scientific objectives.

The project aims to make planetary exploration research more accessible, organized, and evidence-driven. Instead of treating a map as simply a visual representation of Mars, it connects where to explore, why a location matters, what evidence supports it, and how an expedition might reach it.

The development uses Python and relevant data-processing and geospatial tools, alongside web-based technologies for presenting exploration information. The project is designed around publicly available planetary datasets and scientific resources, with an emphasis on traceable evidence and transparent interpretation.

Its creative approach is the integration of planetary science and expedition planning into one decision-support concept. The team considered scientific relevance, dataset availability, geological uncertainty, terrain accessibility, route efficiency, and the distinction between direct observations and scientific interpretations.

The intended impact is to support more informed Mars exploration planning and demonstrate how diverse planetary datasets can be transformed into an understandable scientific expedition framework. It is a research and planning aid, not a certified rover or crew safety-navigation system.
